findings.text: In-memory rate limiter's rateBuckets map never prunes expired entries (only reset when the key is revisited), and the key is clientIP(r) which unconditionally trusts X-Forwarded-For — an unauthenticated attacker rotating the XFF header grows the map without bound → memory exhaustion on /login /auth/refresh /auth/openid. Upstream express-rate-limit MemoryStore sweeps; the unbounded store is a Go-side divergence.

Login/authorize payload built as untyped map[string]any (UserBrowser, loginPayload) and sensitive settings scrubbed by denylist (delete tokenSecret/authOpenIDClientID/...) — any future secret setting not on that list leaks to unauthenticated clients; repo rule prefers internal/wire DTOs; type-assertion dance payload["user"].(map[string]any) repeats the fragility.

rotateSession: on updated == 0 (concurrent rotation lost the race) silently re-reads and returns the current stored refresh token instead of the freshly minted one — uncommented fallback handing caller token state silently.
oidcFailure has a literal no-op branch: `else if status == 400 && message == "No sign-in session" { message = "No sign-in session" }` — dead conditional.

callbackURLIsSafeProviderReturn is a thin wrapper re-running validMobileRedirect — redundant second validation of the same value already checked; the name implies a provider-return check it does not perform.

exchangeAndLoadUserInfo constructs a fresh oidc.NewRemoteKeySet per token exchange (no JWKS caching), and userByOIDCSub does a full-table scan unmarshalling every user's extraData JSON — O(all users) on auth/OIDC-match paths.

Best-effort session cleanup ignores DB errors at refresh-expired/rotated and both logout paths; logout with allDevices skips device wipe when the SELECT fails yet still returns 200 — silent degradation of a security-relevant operation.
responseUser := payload["user"].(map[string]any) + token-embedding sequence copy-pasted across login, refresh, and oidcCallback — three hand-maintained copies of the token contract.
